title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 58 (Refusal of Registration and Appeal Against Refusal)

content.overview: Section 58(1) requires that if a private company limited by shares refuses, whether under its articles or otherwise, to register the transfer of, or the transmission by operation of law of the right to, any securities or interest of a member, it shall within thirty days from delivery of the instrument of transfer or intimation of transmission send notice of the refusal to the transferor and the transferee (or the person giving intimation), giving reasons for such refusal. Section 58(2) provides that the securities or other interest of any member in a public company shall be freely transferable, subject to the proviso that any contract or arrangement between two or more persons in respect of transfer of securities shall be enforceable as a contract. Section 58(3) allows the transferee to appeal to the Tribunal against a private-company refusal within thirty days of receipt of the notice or, if no notice was sent, within sixty days of delivery of the instrument or intimation. Section 58(4) allows the transferee, where a public company without sufficient cause refuses to register the transfer within thirty days of delivery, to appeal within sixty days of such refusal or, where no intimation has been received, within ninety days of delivery. Section 58(5) empowers the Tribunal, after hearing, either to dismiss the appeal or to direct that the transfer or transmission be registered within ten days of receipt of the order, or to direct rectification of the register and payment of damages sustained by any party aggrieved. Section 58(6) makes contravention of a Tribunal order under this section punishable with imprisonment of not less than one year but which may extend to three years and with fine of not less than one lakh rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees.
content.glance: Private company: notice of refusal with reasons within 30 days; public company securities freely transferable (contract proviso); distinct appeal periods for private and public; Tribunal may direct registration within 10 days or rectify + damages; contravention of order attracts imprisonment and fine.
content.study: If a private company limited by shares refuses, whether in pursuance of any power of the company under its articles or otherwise, to register the transfer of, or the transmission by operation of law of the right to, any securities or interest of a member in the company, it shall within a period of thirty days from the date on which the instrument of transfer, or the intimation of such transmission, as the case may be, was delivered to the company, send notice of the refusal to the transferor and the transferee or to the person giving intimation of such transmission, as the case may be, giving reasons for such refusal (s. 58(1)). Without prejudice to sub-section (1), the securities or other interest of any member in a public company shall be freely transferable: Provided that any contract or arrangement between two or more persons in respect of transfer of securities shall be enforceable as a contract (s. 58(2)). The transferee may appeal to the Tribunal against the refusal within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of the notice or in case no notice has been sent by the company, within a period of sixty days from the date on which the instrument of transfer or the intimation of transmission, as the case may be, was delivered to the company (s. 58(3)). If a public company without sufficient cause refuses to register the transfer of securities within a period of thirty days from the date on which the instrument of transfer or the intimation of transmission, as the case may be, is delivered to the company, the transferee may, within a period of sixty days of such refusal or where no intimation has been received from the company, within ninety days of the delivery of the instrument of transfer or intimation of transmission, appeal to the Tribunal (s. 58(4)). The Tribunal, while dealing with an appeal made under sub-section (3) or sub-section (4), may, after hearing the parties, either dismiss the appeal, or by order (a) direct that the transfer or transmission shall be registered by the company and the company shall comply with such order within a period of ten days of the receipt of the order; or (b) direct rectification of the register and also direct the company to pay damages, if any, sustained by any party aggrieved (s. 58(5)). If a person contravenes the order of the Tribunal under this section, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to three years and with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees (s. 58(6)). Current-law framing: identify private vs public company; check the 30-day notice-with-reasons duty for private companies; apply the free-transferability rule and contract proviso for public companies; compute the correct appeal period; seek registration within 10 days or rectification + damages; note the penal consequence of contravening a Tribunal order.

sections.heading: Private company refusal and notice (s. 58(1))
sections.body: If a private company limited by shares refuses (under its articles or otherwise) to register transfer or transmission of securities or interest of a member, it must within thirty days of delivery of the instrument or intimation send notice of refusal to the transferor and the transferee (or person giving intimation), giving reasons for such refusal.

sections.heading: Public company — free transferability (s. 58(2))
sections.body: The securities or other interest of any member in a public company shall be freely transferable. Any contract or arrangement between two or more persons in respect of transfer of securities shall be enforceable as a contract.

sections.heading: Appeal periods (s. 58(3)–(4))
sections.body: Private company: transferee may appeal within 30 days of receipt of notice, or if no notice, within 60 days of delivery of instrument/intimation. Public company without sufficient cause refusing within 30 days: appeal within 60 days of refusal or, if no intimation, within 90 days of delivery.

sections.heading: Tribunal powers (s. 58(5))
sections.body: After hearing, the Tribunal may dismiss the appeal, or direct that the transfer or transmission be registered within ten days of receipt of the order, or direct rectification of the register and payment of damages sustained by any party aggrieved.

sections.heading: Penalty for contravention of Tribunal order (s. 58(6))
sections.body: Contravention of a Tribunal order under this section is punishable with imprisonment of not less than one year but which may extend to three years and with fine of not less than one lakh rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees.

provisions.title: Refusal of registration and appeal against refusal

examples.title: Private company refusal with reasons
examples.body: A private company refuses a transfer under its articles and, within thirty days of delivery of the instrument, sends notice of refusal with reasons to transferor and transferee. The transferee may appeal to the Tribunal under s. 58(3) within thirty days of receipt of the notice.

examples.title: Public company free transferability
examples.body: A public company refuses to register a duly completed transfer without sufficient cause. Section 58(2) makes the securities freely transferable; the transferee may appeal under s. 58(4) within the prescribed period.

examples.title: Tribunal directs registration within 10 days
examples.body: On appeal under s. 58(3) or (4), the Tribunal directs that the transfer be registered and that the company comply within ten days of receipt of the order (s. 58(5)(a)). Non-compliance engages the penalty in s. 58(6).

hypotheticals.question: Does a private company have unlimited power to refuse registration?
hypotheticals.analysis: It may refuse under its articles or otherwise, but must give notice with reasons within thirty days, and the refusal is subject to Tribunal appeal under s. 58(3). The Tribunal may direct registration or rectification and damages.

hypotheticals.question: Are public-company securities always freely transferable?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 58(2) provides that they shall be freely transferable, subject to the proviso that any contract or arrangement between two or more persons in respect of transfer of securities shall be enforceable as a contract. Refusal without sufficient cause is appealable under s. 58(4).

misconceptions.trap: Public companies may freely refuse transfers like private companies.
misconceptions.correction: Section 58(2) provides that securities of a member in a public company shall be freely transferable (subject to enforceable contracts). Refusal without sufficient cause is appealable under s. 58(4).

misconceptions.trap: The appeal period is the same for private and public company refusals.
misconceptions.correction: Private company: 30 days from notice or 60 days from delivery if no notice (s. 58(3)). Public company: 60 days from refusal or 90 days from delivery if no intimation (s. 58(4)).

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 58 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify whether the company is private or public. II. For private company: check whether notice of refusal with reasons was sent within 30 days; compute appeal period under s. 58(3). III. For public company: apply free-transferability under s. 58(2) and the contract proviso; check whether refusal was without sufficient cause within 30 days; compute appeal period under s. 58(4). IV. On appeal, seek registration within 10 days or rectification + damages under s. 58(5). V. Note the penal consequence under s. 58(6) of contravening a Tribunal order. VI. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions on a Section 58 appeal contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Company type (private/public); facts of delivery of instrument/intimation; refusal and notice (or absence of notice/intimation); reasons if given; appeal period calculation; grounds (insufficient cause for public company; improper exercise of articles power for private company); precise relief (registration within 10 days, rectification, damages); identification of parties.

examTips: Private vs public distinction is critical.
Private company: notice of refusal with reasons within 30 days.
Public company: securities freely transferable (contract proviso).
Distinct appeal periods under s. 58(3) and (4).
Tribunal may direct registration within 10 days or rectify + damages; contravention of order is penal under s. 58(6).
revisionPoints: Private company refusal + 30-day notice with reasons (s. 58(1))
